text:
The corrupted element is most likely **M5**, the tail current source. Its width is W=11.63 µm, while its mirror reference M6 is W=2 µm with the same L=1 µm. That implies a 5.8:1 mirror ratio, but the diff pair only draws 10 µA, which matches M5's measured 10.04 µA. A 1:1 mirror would need W≈2 µm. With the oversized device, the tail node sits near ground (Vds=0.019 V, below Vdsat=0.177 V), so M5 is in triode. That pulls the diff-pair sources and the feedback node down, which explains the output error of 1.1 V instead of 1.2 V. The collapsed tail headroom also degrades the loop gain and damping, which fits the undershoot and ringing failures.

M4 (mirror ratio m=3) is the next candidate. It has the largest sensitivity on the error and ringing specs, but its 1:3 ratio is consistent with the measured branch currents (2.5 µA and 7.5 µA), so it is less likely to be the injected fault. M6 is third because it is the reference that sets the M5 mirror ratio, so a wrong M6 width would produce the same mismatch.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M4", "M6"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) width corrupted to W=11.63 um, about 5.8x its mirror reference M6 (W=2 um), instead of a 1:1 mirror. The tail is pushed into triode (Vds=0.019 V < Vdsat=0.177 V), which pulls the diff-pair tail node near ground, shifts the feedback node to about 0.55 V (output 1.1 V, 8.4% error), and degrades loop damping (undershoot and ringing failures). Fix: set M5 W back to 2 um to match M6."}
```
